LESSON: DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING AN INTERVENTION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Action Research
Topic 3.3: Designing and Implementing an Intervention
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Designing and Implementing an Intervention, part of Action Research in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can we implement a comprehensive project plan and ensure continuous improvement through reflective practices?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Designing and Implementing an Intervention together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital Literacy: Learners use digital devices with assistive technology to share reports using charts, posters, videos,

audio visual presentations, the school website, and school social media pages.

Values:
● Respect: Learners accommodate divergent opinions when discussing each proposed solution.

● Unity: Learners display team spirit while working in teams to design a detailed implementation plan.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Online safety: Learners observe online safety as they use digital devices with assistive technology, braille resources or

print resources to share reports using charts, posters, videos, audio visual presentations, the school website, and school

social media pages.

Suggested learning resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology, data collection tools such as observation checklist, internet connectivity,

braille reference materials, print reference materials with appropriate font and colour contrast, print and braille learner’s

books, braille and print writing materials, Scientific talking calculators, scientific calculators with large print and

appropriate colour contrast.

Key skills:

• Analysing the characteristics of action research.

• Using action research to address issues in the community.

• Using data collection tools to record the characteristics of the problem identified.

• Creating an implementation plan focusing on the identified solution.
